subject: Everline renewal: commit uplift + temporary price hold proposal
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Singh <samir.singh@everline.ai>; Nadia Lopez <nadia.lopez@everline.ai>
Cc: Everline Procurement <procurement@everline.ai>
Date: 2026-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Everline renewal: commit uplift + temporary price hold proposal

Hi Samir / Nadia,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — great alignment on product fit and the higher-throughput usage pattern you expect next year. Per our follow-up, I put together an initial commercial proposal that balances your need for predictability with Redwood's unit economics. Summary below, details attached (draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf + current_usage_q2.csv).

Key proposal (high level):
- Commit uplift: 2x annual commit vs. 2025 baseline (effectively a stepped ramp over the first 3 months).
- Pricing: 15% standard renewal discount off list at the new commit level.
- Temporary price hold: lock current unit rate for 90 days post-sign (Q3) to give you runway while you migrate additional traffic.
- Contingent credit: $40,000 one-time credit if realized monthly consumption in Q3 falls below 70% of the committed baseline (payable as invoice credit at quarter close).
- Dedicated capacity option: add-on for sustained low-latency workloads (can be scoped as a separate SKU).

Ask: if this looks directionally OK I can circulate a short Mutual Action Plan and the draft term sheet for procurement/legal. If you prefer stronger pricing in exchange for a longer firm commit (18–24 months), we can structure stepped discounts as an alternative.

Next steps: please confirm which path you prefer (short-term price hold + credit vs. longer-term deeper discount) and who from procurement/legal I should loop for PO/DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to run through the M.A.P.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Samir Singh <samir.singh@everline.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Everline Procurement <procurement@everline.ai>; Nadia Lopez <nadia.lopez@everline.ai>
Date: 2026-06-08T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Everline renewal: commit uplift + temporary price hold proposal

Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear proposal. A few clarifying items from procurement and product: 

1) Procurement needs an explicit multi-month price hold (minimum 6 months) to approve without a larger PO cycle.
2) The $40k contingent credit helps, but given our growth plan we were hoping for a more aggressive renewal discount (20%+) in lieu of a one-off credit.
3) We need clear SLAs on latency for the subset of traffic that routes to our personalization model — if you can include a dedicated capacity add-on price, that would help expedite approval.

Can you share a version of the term sheet that explicitly calls out the price hold duration, the credit trigger mechanics, and an Appendix for the dedicated capacity SKU? I can route to procurement once we have that language.

—Samir
Samir Singh
Head of Platform
Everline.ai
samir.singh@everline.ai | +1 617-555-1199

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Everline renewal — procurement asks (need pricing exception ok)

FYI — Samir pushed for a 6-month price hold and a deeper discount (~20%). Procurement will only sign quickly if we extend the hold. My proposed counter (keeps economics sane):

- Offer: 15% renewal discount at 2x commit (as shared) + $40k contingent credit + 3-month price hold (90 days).
- Elastic concession: if Everline signs a 24-month firm commit we can move to 20% and extend the price hold to 12 months.
- Dedicated capacity: provide published SKU pricing for dedicated pool (per-GPU/month) as an add-on — no credit attached.

Rationale: a 6-month price hold without an additional firm commit materially increases our revenue risk. The contingent credit reduces downside while keeping list-price discipline. Asking for an exception because $40k is above our standard one-off credit band for this segment. 

Can you confirm if you’ll approve the $40k exception and the staged escalation to 20% for a 24-month firm commit? If yes, I’ll update the term sheet (include credit mechanics) and send to Samir + procurement with a MAP and DocuSign link.

Thanks — Olga

Date: 2026-06-08T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Everline renewal — procurement asks (need pricing exception ok)

Olga — thanks for the summary. Approve the $40k credit exception and the 15% renewal discount at 2x commit with a 3-month price hold. Conditions:

- Add clear credit mechanics: credit pays out only if monthly realized consumption < 70% of committed baseline for any month in Q3, and the credit will offset Q4 invoices (not a cash payout).
- Include a pathway to 20% + 12-month hold if Everline signs a 24-month firm commit within 30 days of the renewal signature.
- Add an SLA appendix for the dedicated capacity SKU (latency targets + remediation credits).

Loop Legal for the amendment and get procurement a DocuSign-ready term sheet. David, please help scope the dedicated-capacity appendix (cost per GPU equivalent and target latency windows).

Rishi
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Singh <samir.singh@everline.ai>
Cc: Everline Procurement <procurement@everline.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-09T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Everline renewal — updated term sheet and MAP (DocuSign link)

Samir — thanks for the prompt feedback. Based on internal approval, attached is an updated term sheet (redlined_term_sheet_final.pdf) and a short Mutual Action Plan that reflects the concessions below. I also included our Q2 usage export (current_usage_q2.csv) for your SOW/finance reviews.

Confirmed commercial terms (summary):
- Commit: 2x baseline (annualized) with a staged ramp in months 1–3.
- Renewal discount: 15% at the new commit level.
- Temporary price hold: 90 days from signature (Q3).
- Contingent credit: $40,000 one-time credit, payable as invoice offset per the credit mechanics below.
- Upsell pathway: 20% discount + 12-month price hold if Everline executes a 24-month firm commit within 30 days of signature.
- Dedicated capacity add-on: Appendix A in the attached term sheet (per-GPU/month SKU and latency SLA).

Credit mechanics (excerpt):
- Trigger: any month during Q3 where realized consumption < 70% of the committed monthly baseline.
- Remedy: credit applied to subsequent Redwood invoices (cannot be redeemed for cash).
- Documentation: usage verified from Redwood’s billing/usage export (attached).

I created a short Mutual Action Plan in the term sheet and prepared a DocuSign envelope for signatures to speed procurement: https://docusign.com/placeholder/everline-renewal-2026.

If that looks good, please confirm by EOD and procurement can route the PO. Happy to set a 20-minute call today to walk procurement through the credit trigger language.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
